acceptance: Each managed vendor with published results has a row: the clause, its source and date read, and the owner's decision.
Any result the owner decides to withdraw is handled through the existing takedown process, not by editing pages.
context: Listed for the owner; see also human-action-required. Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.
description:
Problem: the published corpus includes results for Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and other managed services. No document in the repository records whether each vendor's terms allow publishing benchmark results; docs/tpc-licensing-analysis.md covers redistributing the TPC tools, not publishing results. The results are already public in the static summaries and bundle files, and static result pages will make each one indexable.

Outcome: a short record, per vendor in the corpus, of what its terms say about publishing benchmark results and what BenchBox does about it. This is a legal judgement for the owner; an agent can gather the texts but must not decide.

Owner decision (2026-11-13): static result pages include every published result meanwhile.
